items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S657

SPONSOR: MYRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, the education law, the civil practice
law and rules, and the state finance law, in relation to regulating
public data maintained by county and city boards of elections and estab-
lishing the New York voting and elections database and institute to
maintain a statewide database of voting and election data

 
PURPOSE:

To create a New York State Voting and Elections Database and Institute
which will compile New York's election data and administer it for
research and to provide election operation. Assistance and Lion to poli-
tical subdivisions as well as the public.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the election law by adding a new section 3-112 which
requires the State Board of Elections to distribute, within a reasonable
amount of time, election results, voter history, voter registration
lists, district maps, poll sites, and early voting site maps from their
respective counties and cities using a standard method to a statewide
database.

Section 2 amends Title 7 of the education law by adding article 117
creating the New York Voting Elections Database and Institute which
establish a central institution to reduce the burden on boards of
elections, local governments and school districts by partnering with the
State University of New York and City University of New York to maintain
and administer to the public, election and voting data from one
location. The Database and Institute will provide resources to voters
for training and information on voting systems and election adminis-
tration. The Database and Institute will be in electronic form and
provide information to the public online of the previous twelve year
period of total population estimates, district level election results,
voter statistics, election day or early voting poll sites, districting
or re-distring plans, and any information relating to race, color, and
language minority groups.

Section 3 amends the civil practice law to create a new rule 4550 which
creates a rebuttable presumption that data or information maintained by
the Institute is valid in court.

Section 4 amends the education law by adding a new section 2614 which
requires school districts to transmit election data for school board
elections to the Institute within 90 days of each election.

Section 5 amends section 2038 of the education law renumbering section
2039 and a new section 2038 which requires school districts to transmit
election data for school board elections to the Institute within 90 days
of each election.

Section 6 amends section 2553 of the education law by adding a new
subdivision 2-a which requires school districts to transmit election
data for school board elections to the Institute within 90 days of each
election.
Section 7 amends the state finance law by adding a new section 97-k
which establishes the New York Voting and Elections Database and Insti-
tute fund under joint custody of the State Comptroller and the Commis-
sioner of Taxation and Finance consisting of all public or private funds
used for maintenance of the database and for research conducted by the
Institute.

Section 8 provides for the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The database will provide stakeholders across the state with access to
reliable data and state-of-the-art analysis on voting and elections in
New York. This would benefit New York State by reducing the burden on
boards of elections and local governments that currently have to respond
to a constant stream of FOIA requests for election data and information
that can and should be centrally maintained, reducing the burden and
expense of voting rights litigation by providing a neutral and robust
set of data upon which all parties can rely, encouraging the state and
municipalities to enact evidence-backed policies that will assist
election officials in evaluating the extent to which current practices
favor expansive access to the franchise, and improving transparency
which will. allow voters to detect inequitable policies and racial
discrimination.

Furthermore, this database will be operated by a collaboration between
the City University of New York and the State University of New York
systems, which will provide a unique opportunity for students to learn
about the mechanics and operations of elections through supporting the
database by cleaning, archiving, and analyzing election data.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S8202 of 2022: Passed Senate.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S657AREVISED 1/23/24

SPONSOR: MYRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, the education law, the civil practice
law and rules and the state finance law, in relation to regulating
public data maintained by county and city boards of elections and estab-
lishing the New York voting and elections academic center to maintain a
statewide database of voting and election data

 
PURPOSE:

To create a New York State Voting and Elections Database in the State
Board of Elections and an Academic Center which will compile New York's
election data and administer it for research and to provide election
operation assistance to political subdivisions as well as the public.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 names the Bill in honor of Dr. John Flateau, a voting rights
advocate and Professor at Medgar Evers College.

Section 2 requires local boards of elections to transmit election data
to a publicly accessible statewide database operated by SBOE. This data
includes election results at the election district level, information on
affidavit and absentee ballot usage, voter files and registration
lists,maps/shapefiles of districts, and lists of poll sites. Jurisdic-
tions must send this information by January 1 after the election or
within 10 business days, whichever is later. SBOE would then have 60
days to post this information to the online database (except for indi-
vidual voter registration records). It also orders the SBOE to promul-
gate regulations for processing data requests for the election data and
gives SBOE, the Attorney General (OAG), and co-directors of the Academic
Center the ability to bring legal actions against non-compliant juris-
dictions after six months of non-compliance. If a jurisdiction is deemed
non-compliant three times within a five-year period they will be put
under NYVRA preclearance and changes to their election policies and
practices will be subject to AG or court approval.

Section 3 amends the Education Law to establish the New York Voting and
Elections Academic Center ("Center") and specifies its functions.  The
Center must maintain data covering the previous 12 years and must make
all data (except data which would identify an individual) available to
the public for free online. It must also maintain estimates of citizens
of voting age who speak a language other than English and publish the
list of each jurisdiction required to provide language assistance (as
well as which languages for each jurisdiction) in order to facilitate
compliance with language requirements of the NYVRA. The Center must
submit an annual report summarizing its activities, progress, and
finances to the executive and legislative leaders.

Section 4 amends the Civil Practice Law to create a rebuttable presump-
tion that data or information maintained by the Institute is valid in
court.

Sections 5, 6, and 7 amend the Education Law to order school districts
to submit the same kinds of election data as municipalities to the data-
base.
Section B amends the Election law to require villages running their own
elections to transmit the same data as other municipalities.

Section 9 of the bill amends the State Finance Law to establish the New
York Voting and Elections Database and Academic Fund ("fund").  This
fund will be under the joint custody of the State Comptroller and the
Commissioner of Taxation and Finance. It orders that the fund consist of
all public or private funds used for the maintenance of the database and
research conducted by the Institute. It allows the money in the fund to
be invested by the comptroller but prevents the money in the fund from
being commingled with any other fund or account for investment purposes.
It also allows money in the fund to be used for database maintenance and
research and education programs after appropriation by the legislature.

Section 10 allows the AG to adopt the Center's list of language coverage
requirements and to issue any relevant regulations.

Section 11 provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:;

The database will provide stakeholders across the state with access to
reliable data and state-of-the-art analysis on voting and elections in
New York. This would benefit New York State by reducing the burden on
boards of elections and local governments that currently have to respond
to a constant stream of FOIA requests for election data and information
that can and should be centrally maintained, reducing the burden and
expense of voting rights litigation by providing a neutral and robust
set of data upon which all parties can rely, encouraging the state and
municipalities to enact evidence-based policies that will assist
election officials in evaluating the extent to which current practices
favor expansive access to the franchise, and improving transparency
which will allow voters to detect inequitable policies and racial
discrimination.

Furthermore, the academic center will be operated by a collaboration
between the City University of New York and the State University of New
York systems, which will provide a unique opportunity for students to
learn about the mechanics and operations of elections through supporting
the database by cleaning, archiving, and analyzing election data.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S8202 of 2022: Passed Senate.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
April 1, 2026.

summary: Enacts the "Doctor John L. Flateau Voting and Elections Database and Academic Center of New York Act"; regulates public data maintained by county and city boards of elections; establishes the New York voting and elections academic center to maintain a statewide database of voting and election data.
